🟠 3p% on attempts after an offensive rebound are typically better than 🔵 3p% on the first shot of a possession. 

This season, 2022-23, and 2010-11 teams have actually shot worse on 3-pointers after an offensive rebound.

NBA league average 3p% this century
First Shot: 35.68%	
Second Chance: 36.58%

images.alt:
A dumbbell chart titled "Threes After an Offensive Rebound Go In More Often." The subtitle reads "NBA First-shot 3P% vs. Second-chance 3P% each season," with first shot in blue and second chance in orange. Two notes explain: "First-shot 3P% = 3P% on threes taken on the first shot of a possession. Second-chance 3P% = 3P% on threes taken after an offensive rebound."

Each row is a season, with a blue dot for first-shot 3P%, an orange dot for second-chance 3P%, and a bar between them. The gap is listed on the right, orange when second chance is higher and blue when first shot is higher. The x-axis runs from 34% to 39%.

A highlighted summary row at the top shows all seasons combined: first shot 35.7%, second chance 36.6%, a gap of +0.9.

Gaps by season, newest to oldest: 2026-27 so far −0.5, 2025-26 +1.5, 2024-25 +1.2, 2023-24 +0.5, 2022-23 −0.7, 2021-22 +0.4, 2020-21 +0.9, 2019-20 +0.1, 2018-19 +0.6, 2017-18 +0.6, 2016-17 +1.3, 2015-16 +1.3, 2014-15 +0.7, 2013-14 +1.7, 2012-13 +1.0, 2011-12 +0.6, 2010-11 −0.3, 2009-10 +1.4, 2008-09 +0.4, 2007-08 +0.8, 2006-07 +3.1, 2005-06 +1.3, 2004-05 +1.1, 2003-04 +1.9, 2002-03 +2.4, 2001-02 +1.6, 2000-01 +1.3.

Second-chance threes went in more often in 24 of the 26 full seasons. The biggest gap was 2006-07 at +3.1. First shot was higher only in 2010-11, 2022-23 and so far in 2026-27.

items.author: Hoop Informatics
items.body_excerpt:
3-point volume vs 3-point accuracy after offensive rebounds.

I must caution the sample size. Teams have only taken 500-800 total 3-pointers this season & that’s still too small a sample. It’s takes around 27 games for team total 3p% to stabilize. 

Here we are looking at only 31-115 total attempts.

images.alt:
A scatter plot titled "Kicking Out, and Hitting?" with the subtitle "How often each team shoots threes after offensive rebounds, and how well they make them." A note says 3-point percentage is based on only 31 to 115 attempts per team, which is a very small sample size and very noisy data. Team logos are the points. The horizontal axis is 3-point attempts per 100 second-chance possessions, with more threes to the right. The vertical axis is 3-point percentage after offensive rebounds, with better shooting toward the top. Gray dashed lines mark the league averages of 32.7 attempts and 34.6%, splitting the chart into four corners labeled "High volume, high accuracy" (top right), "Low volume, high accuracy" (top left), "High volume, low accuracy" (bottom right) and "Low volume, low accuracy" (bottom left).
